evidence.title: README.md
evidence.locator: Quick Start; Web Dashboard; MCP; RObot; FAQ
evidence.finding: Ralph offers CLI/TUI loops, an alpha web dashboard, workspace-scoped MCP server, planning documents, backend selection and Telegram intervention.

evidence.title: docs/guide/backends.md
evidence.locator: Supported Backends; Backend Setup; Per-Hat Backend Override
evidence.finding: Names Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Pi among eleven backends, documents native Claude login and API keys, and per-hat backend overrides.

evidence.title: docs/guide/cli-reference.md
evidence.locator: ralph run; loops; tools memory; tools task
evidence.finding: CLI documents bounded iterations, headless execution, recording, continuation, loop logs/diff/rebase/resume, and memory/task operations.

evidence.title: docs/advanced/parallel-loops.md
evidence.locator: How It Works; Loop States; Auto-Merge Workflow; Remote Review Workflow
evidence.finding: Concurrent loops have worktrees, separate events/tasks and shared memories. Completed work can enter a merge queue or publish remote review branches; failed merges need review.

evidence.title: docs/guide/configuration.md
evidence.finding: Configuration defines iteration/runtime limits, inactivity timeouts, hook timeouts and per-hat activation limits.

evidence.title: docs/advanced/memory-system.md
evidence.finding: Memories persist across sessions in .agent/memories.md and include codebase patterns, decisions and recurring solutions.

evidence.title: docs/concepts/backpressure.md
evidence.locator: In Hat Instructions; Implementing Backpressure; Anti-Patterns
evidence.finding: Documents test/lint/typecheck evidence and reviewer hats, but warns that emitted evidence can be fake. Instructional examples are not proof of enforcement.

evidence.finding: The repository grants the application source under MIT.

locations.result: Searched the repository documentation tree for an official roadmap. Design/proposal files and open PRs are not treated as shipped.

Scanned 30 recent public issues/PRs. Examples: Give review hats a fresh context (the scratchpad is shared by default); Record the model and backend args that served each iteration; `hats.<hat>.timeout` bounds only wave workers, not a sequential activation. These are leads, not proven restrictions or shipped capabilities.

gaps: The production-deployment, security and cost-management guides contain Python-era examples inconsistent with the current Rust CLI; they do not establish current costs, sandbox guarantees or remote persistence.
Open issue 412 questions sequential per-hat timeouts; no per-tool-call cap or successful enforcement test is claimed.
No accepted native PR-creation or supervising-agent delegation capability was established. Open requests are not future release promises.
